precepts.text: Paul, rebuked for reviling God's high priest, cited this law: it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
precepts.point: Acts 23 is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
Acts 23 is the example. Paul stood before the council, and “the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth. Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?”

“And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest? Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.” Paul quoted this very verse. Reviling the gods and cursing the ruler of thy people is speaking evil of the ruler, and Paul owned the law the moment he knew who he had spoken to.

precepts.why:
“For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.”

The Sadducees were grieved that the apostles preached the resurrection, and they did not even believe in it. They were the upper class, the wealthy priestly and merchant families, moved by political and economic position. They came under the influence of Hellenism the same way today's pastors come under the influence of Americanism, preaching a prosperity and a political gospel and adopting their own man-made traditions.

They were grieved because the teaching pulled the people, the money and the control away from them. It is jealousy, envy, and the inability to guide the people.

points: The high priest commanded them to smite Paul on the mouth after he spoke out of place in front of the elders and the scribes and Pharisees.

Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people: so Paul repented of that, because he didn't know he was the high priest. During this time, it was not lawful, but they did it anyway: they had two high priests. Paul probably knew about the other high priest.

I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: Paul confessed he was the son of a Pharisee, a Benjamite from the tribe of Benjamin. He noticed that the crowd was Pharisees and Sadducees, so he took advantage of that and said, hey, I'm a Pharisee, and that's what caused a split amongst the council.
The Pharisees and Sadducees make up three tribes: Judah, Benjamin and Levi. Paul was a Benjamite, but he was a Pharisee. But the high priest only and always was of the tribe of Levi.
The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both. That's what caused the split and the confusion between the two.
The Sadducees believe in no resurrection or spirit, but the Pharisees confess both, meaning they believe in the resurrection, and Paul used that to his advantage to get the Pharisees on his side.
Because a lot of time Israel get it twisted. Oh, yeah, I'm unified. I wear purple. I'm unified. I wear fringes. I'm unified. No, my dear. No. Unification start with the mind.

I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day: so you got to ask yourself that. If you're living in good conscience before God and men until this day, you are unified with your people. If you're not doing that, you are not unified with your people. And such behavior encourage a traitor behavior.
